headline: Several wounded as attack hits Riyadh airport, Biman suspends flights
summary: King Khalid International Airport operations were temporarily halted following a blast, leading Biman Bangladesh to suspend its Dhaka-Riyadh flights until further notice.
details: Several people were injured in an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday afternoon. The General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) confirmed that airport operations were temporarily suspended as a precautionary measure.

Authorities are currently assessing the damage and verifying the security of the facilities. The exact number of casualties has not yet been confirmed, and the condition of the injured remains unknown.
In response to the security situation, Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended its flights between Dhaka and Riyadh until further notice.

This incident follows a series of attacks on Saudi aviation facilities. Earlier this week, Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for attacks that killed three Saudi citizens, including a pilot, and injured others.
The Houthi group stated that these attacks are a response to Saudi aggression in Yemen, claiming that 60 air and missile strikes were launched in Yemen within a 24-hour period.

Previous attacks on October 6 and 7 also resulted in deaths at Abha International Airport and King Khalid Airport, signaling an escalation in conflict between Houthi forces and the Saudi-backed government.

In response to the security situation, Biman Bangladesh Airlines has suspended its flights between Dhaka and Riyadh until further notice.

headline_marked: BNP tells activists to [[ensure peaceful Durga Puja]] nationwide
headline: BNP tells activists to ensure peaceful Durga Puja nationwide
summary: The party has instructed leaders and activists to remain vigilant and coordinate with local puja committees to prevent any disruptions to the festival.
details: The BNP leadership has instructed party leaders and activists to remain vigilant to ensure peaceful Durga Puja celebrations nationwide and prevent any attempts to disrupt the festival.
A 12-member central monitoring committee was formed on October 9 to oversee the festival. Party volunteers will coordinate with local puja committees at venues across the country.
BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi stated that the main focus is to share the joy of Puja with everyone and urged party members to stay vigilant against propaganda.

During a National Standing Committee meeting chaired by Tarique Rahman, leaders also expressed concern over the rising prices of essential goods and called for tighter market supervision to combat syndicates.
The committee discussed other urgent issues, including the the growing drug problem, waste management, and the response to dengue outbreaks.
Additionally, Tarique Rahman called a meeting of the BNP parliamentary party to address party discipline, law and order, and allegations of land grabbing and extortion involving some party members.
The party has already taken action against several members, including the expulsion of 14 leaders and activists and the dissolution of three committees following irregularities.
caption:
BNP activists are being deployed as 'sleepless sentinels' to ensure a peaceful Durga Puja across Bangladesh.

The BNP leadership has instructed party leaders and activists to remain vigilant to ensure peaceful Durga Puja celebrations nationwide and prevent any attempts to disrupt the festival.

A 12-member central monitoring committee was formed on October 9 to oversee the festival. Party volunteers will coordinate with local puja committees at venues across the country.

BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi stated that the main focus is to share the joy of Puja with everyone and urged party members to stay vigilant against propaganda.

During a National Standing Committee meeting chaired by Tarique Rahman, leaders also expressed concern over the rising prices of essential goods and called for tighter market supervision to combat syndicates.

The committee discussed other urgent issues, including the the growing drug problem, waste management, and the response to dengue outbreaks.

Additionally, Tarique Rahman called a meeting of the BNP parliamentary party to address party discipline, law and order, and allegations of land grabbing and extortion involving some party members.

The party has already taken action against several members, including the expulsion of 14 leaders and activists and the dissolution of three committees following irregularities.
